Write the mortality review cards and their index

Source: R/build_mortality_cards.R
build_mortality_cards.Rd

Writes one self-contained HTML card per animal, and an index page, into dir. A card shows the animal's facts (species, size, tag, release, last detection, the candidate death date and its basis, the deciding rule and every rule stream's vote), a map of the station positions that heard it with the trail of its daily detection-weighted centroid, and time panels on one axis: detections per day by station (one row per station_id; a station whose deployments moved has one row and several positions on the map), detections per day, apparent movement, depth, acceleration (or the sensor the tag carries), one evidence lane per rule stream and the reviewer's day notes. A day scrubber with play, speed and a trailing window drives the map. The reviewer calls each animal alive, dead_or_shed or uncertain, sets or types a death date and writes a note; calls are kept in the browser, keyed by animal_id, and exported as one CSV for apply_mortality_calls().

Usage

build_mortality_cards(
  x,
  bands,
  dir,
  which = c("dead", "review"),
  all = FALSE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

x

The detset the bands were computed from.

bands

The result of detect_mortality().

dir

Folder for index.html and the cards folder. It is created if needed; existing cards in it are replaced.

which

Bands that get a card. The index lists every animal.

all

If TRUE, every band gets a card, as which = c("dead", "review", "alive") does.

control

A list of options: title for the index; store, the key of the browser store, which keeps calls apart between studies (the default is built from a hash of the full path of dir, so two folders named review in different studies do not share calls, and a rebuild in the same folder keeps them); outline, an sf polygon in WGS 84 drawn under the stations (needs the sf package); cores, the number of processes that write cards (the default is the option detqc.cores, or 1; above 1 the cards are written by parallel::mclapply(), which runs one process on Windows).

Value

x, invisibly, with one log record and x$cards: a data frame with one row per card (animal_id, band, file, bytes, checked

and failed), whose attribute index holds the path of index.html.

Details

Size is any length, weight or mass column of the animals table, shown under the column's name. The table contract carries no unit for size, so the card prints a unit only when the animals table states one: a unit suffix on the column name (length_mm gives "length 400 mm") or a column named after it with _unit (length and length_unit). Otherwise the value is followed by "(unit as recorded)", the unit of the file it was read from.

The index groups the animals by band, with progress per band, a search box, a sidebar that follows the scroll, and buttons that export and import every call. Inside the review band, animals are ordered by the persistence score of the bands when it is present, highest first.

The cards and the index load nothing from the network. After the cards are written, each card file is read back from disk and its numbers are compared with the detset, the animals table and the bands by code that shares nothing with the card writer. Each of these must be equal: detections and detection days, the detections of every day, the first and last day, the stations and the detections of every day at each station, the list of stations, the located detections of every day at each position, the depth and sensor days with their daily median and 5th and 95th percentiles, the band, the candidate date, the votes, release, expiry, the days from the last detection to the data horizon, and species. A card that disagrees is kept, marked checked = FALSE with the quantities in failed, and named in a warning.

A card's time axis starts at the release, or at the first day of the detset when the release is earlier, so a card built from one month of a long study does not draw years with no data. The cursor opens on the animal's first day with a detection, so the first map shows where it was heard; an animal first heard weeks into the detset opened on an empty map. The map opens on the stations that heard the animal when they fill less than a quarter of the array's extent; a button switches to the whole array. The D key, or the dead/shed button, stamps the candidate death date when no date is set, never the day in view. The candidate is the first detection of the final run; where the site stopped listening before the run, its basis gives the detection before the run as the earliest the death could be (see detect_mortality()). Where the sensor panels show a later death, set the date from them. With no candidate, the call is saved without a date and the card stays open and asks for one: move the cursor to the death day and press X (or "= cursor"), or type the date. X moves a date already set.

See also

review_mortality(), apply_mortality_calls()

Examples

study <- example_mortality
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
mort_rules <- mortality_rules(min_days = 3, min_calendar_days = 3)
bands <- detect_mortality(dets, rules = mort_rules)
dets <- build_mortality_cards(dets, bands, file.path(tempdir(), "review"))
dets$cards[, c("animal_id", "band", "bytes", "checked")]
#>   animal_id   band bytes checked
#> 1     ST-01 review 70140    TRUE
#> 2     ST-02 review 69923    TRUE
#> 3     ST-03 review 69962    TRUE
#> 4     ST-04 review 69970    TRUE
